data.title: FondCircle Unveils New Physician-Co-Branded N1 Digital Otoscope at HLTH USA 2026
data.description:
Developed with ENT specialist Dr. John Boone, the smartphone-connected ear camera launches in January 2027 alongside FondCircle's Black Friday event.

LAS VEGAS, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Connected home health brand FondCircle wrapped up its debut appearance at HLTH USA 2026 (held November 15–18 at The Venetian Expo in Las Vegas) by announcing a long-term strategic partnership with board-certified otolaryngologist Dr. John Boone and unveiling its first physician-co-branded device, the N1 digital otoscope. Scheduled to launch on Amazon and fondcircle.com in January 2027, the N1 brings real-time ear canal visualization directly to consumers' smartphones.

Dr. Boone, who serves as FondCircle's medical director, brings more than a decade of clinical experience treating both adults and children, alongside his background as founder of PrimaryENT in Minnesota and founder and CEO of EUC. Through this multi-year collaboration, Dr. Boone provides clinical insight and physician-informed design input across FondCircle's expanding product roadmap.

"Parents and caregivers often feel anxious when ear discomfort strikes at home, yet they lack simple ways to see what is happening or share clear visuals with a healthcare provider," said Dr. John Boone. "Working with FondCircle on the N1 allowed us to focus on practical, everyday usability—giving families an accessible tool for visual documentation and better-informed conversations with their doctors."

Designed for convenient home observation and record-keeping rather than medical diagnosis, the N1 digital otoscope (model FMC-N1) connects directly to compatible USB-C mobile devices—supporting both iOS (iPhone 15 series and newer) and USB-C Android smartphones—to stream live video inside the FondCircle App. Users can capture high-clarity photos and video clips to track changes over time, assisted by six built-in LEDs with on-device adjustable brightness controls.

Alongside the N1 preview, FondCircle's exhibit offered attendees hands-on demonstrations of its flagship home monitoring lineup, all unified within the FondCircle App so households can track longitudinal trends and share selected readings with family members or caregivers:

  • A2 Upper-Arm Blood Pressure Monitor: Clinically validated for blood pressure measurement during pregnancy and in adults with diabetes through separate accuracy studies meeting ISO 81060-2 standards. Features a 5.7-inch display with a built-in seven-day trend chart and optional spoken readings.
  • A3 Upper-Arm Blood Pressure Monitor: Equipped with TripleCheck technology, which automatically captures three consecutive readings and calculates an average, complete with Bluetooth syncing to the FondCircle App.
  • F3 Body Fat Analyzer: Tracks 15 body composition metrics via the FondCircle App while cycling through seven core readings directly on its onboard color display.
  • D1 Infrared Thermometer: Delivers forehead and ear temperature readings in under one second, featuring a fever-indicating color-coded screen and a silent mode for nighttime checks on sleeping children.

During the conference, FondCircle founder and CEO James Sun also joined attendees on the show floor to share the company's founding vision of making everyday health monitoring less intimidating for modern households.

"Home health devices shouldn't feel cold, complicated, or disconnected from real life," said James Sun, founder and CEO of FondCircle. "Our debut at HLTH USA and our partnership with Dr. Boone reflect our commitment to pairing clinical perspective with intuitive design that empowers families every day."

Holiday Savings Event Underway

As the holiday shopping season kicks off, FondCircle is running its Black Friday Savings Event through November 30, 2026, offering up to 50% off select devices and free U.S. shipping sitewide at fondcircle.com/pages/black-friday and Amazon.

For ongoing updates on the N1 digital otoscope ahead of its January 2027 retail debut, visit fondcircle.com/pages/hlth-2026.

About FondCircle

FondCircle develops connected home health monitoring devices designed to make everyday health tracking simpler and more accessible. Its ecosystem spans blood pressure monitors, body composition scales, infrared thermometers, blood glucose meters, and pulse oximeters, all integrated through the FondCircle App to help users organize readings, monitor trends, and share records with loved ones and caregivers. Learn more at fondcircle.com.

data.title: GLOBAL MARKETS-Asian stocks rally as Huang's Nvidia return revives AI trade
data.description:
* Asian shares tracking US higher as markets cheer on Huang's return

* Taiex leads charge with more than 9% gain

* Treasury yields, dollar climb as Fed rate hike bets grow

By Jiaxing Li

HONG KONG, Nov 24 (Reuters) - Asian shares leapt on Tuesday following a spectacular Wall Street surge as Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO sparked a relief rally in the battered AI trade, while Federal Reserve tightening bets lifted Treasury yields and the dollar.

MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan climbed 4.6%, bouncing back from an eight-month low and heading for its biggest single-day gain since July 31.

Japan's Nikkei added 4.5% as traders returned from a local holiday. South Korea's KOSPI surged 7.5%, while Taiwanese shares jumped 9.1%.

Huang's comeback capped a whirlwind week of events that whipped markets and tore through the AI ecosystem, which has relied on Nvidia ( NVDA ) for everything from supplying chips to bankrolling the industry's massive buildout.

Shares of Nvidia ( NVDA ) surged 31.5% on Monday, marking their biggest daily percentage gain in 23 years and restoring nearly $1 trillion in value to the company.

Companies across the AI industry also rallied sharply, with the Nasdaq 100, which is concentrated in megacap tech companies, jumping more than 6%.

"The return of the most important man in the AI industry to the helm of its most important company has eased fear and uncertainty about the AI trade, at least at the margins," despite lingering concerns about slowing AI investment and moderating earnings growth, said Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com.

There are other risks for the market as well, such as uncertainty over US interest rate policy, with investors set to focus on Wednesday's PCE Index data ahead of the Fed's final meeting of 2026, he added.

S&P 500 futures were flat and Nasdaq futures edged down 0.2% early on Tuesday. The cash S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite indexes surged 4.7% and 6.5%, respectively.

AI REBOUND LIFTS FED TIGHTENING BETS

The sharp AI rebound has also eased growth concerns and loosened financial conditions, reviving market bets for near-term Fed tightening and lifting front-end Treasury yields and the dollar.

Fed funds futures traders are now pricing in a hike at the Fed's December meeting as a certainty, compared with 89% odds on Friday, when stocks tumbled, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool. The market-implied chance of a supersized 50-basis-point increase in around 5%.

The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note rose for a second day and was last at 4.94%, and the yield on the 2-year note rose to 4.69%. The dollar, meanwhile, hovered near a more than 19-month high against the euro.

In commodities, oil prices fell more than 3% to near a three-month low on rising supplies from the Middle East, which offset worries about shipping and refinery attacks in the region. Brent crude futures were flat at $89.50 a barrel after settling down 3.5% at $89.37 a barrel on Monday.

Bullion recovered from a more than one-year low, with spot gold last up 0.7% at $3,657.97 per ounce as investors bought the dip.

data.title: Huang returns as Nvidia CEO after Trump intervention in abrupt board reversal
data.description:
Nov 23 (Reuters) - Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO on Monday under pressure from US President Donald Trump, a stunning reversal following his resignation over revelations of extramarital affairs, drawing approval from Wall Street and opposition from US lawmakers.

Huang's comeback caps a whirlwind week of events that roiled markets and tore through the AI ecosystem that has relied on Nvidia for everything from supplying chips to bankrolling the industry's massive buildout.

But the board's about-face - less than a week after Chair Harvey Jones said Nvidia would not rehire Huang as CEO because his personal behavior was inconsistent with the company's code of conduct - raises questions about its independence, governance experts said, even as the company's investigation remains unfinished.

Huang's comeback boosted Wall Street and sent Nvidia's shares soaring. The stock closed up 31.5%, adding nearly $1 trillion in market value, vaulting the chipmaker back to the position of the second-biggest company by market value after Apple. The gains were not enough, however, to erase all losses since Huang's resignation on November 12.

Nvidia said in a statement that based on US government input the board was confident that "Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk," a claim backed by Trump in an interview with CNBC.

Huang said in a statement that he was honored to return and "can't wait to get back to work." He returned to company headquarters to cheers from employees and said he was going to "be a better CEO the second time around," Business Insider reported, citing a person familiar with the matter.

"Jensen's return is not a total shock, but it does send a troubling message about the state of corporate governance in America," said James St. Aubin, chief investment officer at Ocean Park Asset Management. "Certain executives are going to be held to different standards if you are perceived to be a one of one," he said, adding Huang would still have to answer "some tough questions from Congress."

Lawmakers across party lines strongly objected to Huang's reinstatement and called on Congress to pass the Chip Security Act, a bill that seeks to stop legally exported advanced chips from being diverted to China, where their sales are restricted.

US Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer said Trump was "putting his own financial interests ... before our national security," while Senator Pete Ricketts, a Nebraska Republican, said Huang's return "doesn't absolve Nvidia of answering for national security concerns and unaccounted-for chips."

TRUMP'S SUPPORT FOR HUANG

Huang returned at the strong urging of Trump, industry leaders including Elon Musk, and some investors. His departure had reverberated from Silicon Valley to Taipei. A petition calling for his reinstatement drew more than 180,000 signatures, underscoring the unusually strong support for an executive who stepped down amid controversy.

"I believe my intervention was very important to get Jensen Huang back," Trump told CNBC.

Trump owns between $11 million and $55 million in Nvidia stock, according to a Reuters review of his annual financial disclosure for 2025 and share trading disclosures for 2026. Monday's surge in Nvidia shares could have boosted Trump's net worth by as much as $17 million. A White House spokesperson said Trump's stock and bond portfolio was independently managed by third-party financial institutions and neither the president nor any member of his family had any ability to direct or influence how the portfolio was invested.

Nvidia's board did not mention Huang's affairs. Apart from Alice Huang, the Chinese businesswoman who is accused of having ties with Beijing, Huang is accused of having had intimate relationships with at least two Nvidia employees.

Jensen Huang has acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife and apologized, but has not publicly addressed the individual alleged relationships in detail. China has denied the espionage allegations. Attempts by Reuters to reach Alice Huang have been unsuccessful.

"There were definitely a lot of people who wanted him back. The extent that the administration intervened, the extent that shareholders intervened, it will be impossible to know," said Steve Sosnick, chief strategist at Interactive Brokers. "But it tells us to some extent that Jensen Huang was too big to be fired."

CHINA IS KEY TO NVIDIA

The moves come as Nvidia faces heightened scrutiny in Washington over the flow of advanced AI chips to China. US authorities have tightened licensing rules for some chip shipments and overseas data centers serving Chinese companies, while lawmakers are preparing to question Huang, who has pushed for greater access to the Chinese market.

Huang has agreed to testify before the US Senate in a public hearing on December 3, the Senate Banking Committee said. Huang's personal spokesperson declined to comment.

Trump told CNBC that he had urged Nvidia to continue reviewing its compliance with US export controls to ensure it was adequately protecting national security. Trump, who visited Shenzhen last week, told CNBC he had spoken to Chinese President Xi Jinping about Huang.

Huang's exit from Nvidia threatened its business in China, Reuters reported on Monday, with some customers there cancelling or hesitating to place orders, jeopardizing billions in revenue.

The US on Monday was set to add Singapore-based chip firm Megaspeed, which is closely tied to an espionage investigation involving Nvidia, to its trade blacklist, a person familiar with the matter told Reuters.

The Nvidia board has formed a committee to investigate whether foreign intelligence efforts targeted Huang and another committee focused on national security and export controls.

The company is also facing multiple investigations over issues ranging from potential accounting irregularities to suspected chip smuggling, and a shareholder lawsuit accusing the company and Huang of defrauding shareholders by concealing Huang's relationship with Alice Huang.

(Reporting by Anhata Rooprai and Deborah Sophia in Bengaluru and David Morgan in Washington; Additional reporting Saqib Ahmed, Chibuike Oguh, and Tom Bergin; Writing by Sayantani Ghosh; Editing by Anil D'Silva, Saumyadeb Chakrabarty and Matthew Lewis)

data.title: Japan's Nikkei rises over 4% after Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO
data.description:
(Adds share moves, details and analysts' comments)

By Satoshi Sugiyama

TOKYO, Nov 24 (Reuters) - Japan's Nikkei share average climbed more than 4% on Tuesday, tracking a sharp rally on Wall Street as Nvidia's ( NVDA ) decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO rekindled investor enthusiasm for the AI trade.

The Nikkei 225 Index advanced 4.62% to 59,045.30, rebounding from a 5% slump on Friday. The broader Topix climbed 2.8% to 3,777.21, reversing a nearly 4% drop posted on Friday. Tokyo markets were closed on Monday for a public holiday.

"Such positive news has provided a good pretext for buying back shares. Because the market had fallen so sharply, the short-covering rebound is also proving large," said Masahiro Ichikawa, chief market strategist at Sumitomo Mitsui DS Asset Management.

AI- and chip-related shares led the Nikkei's rally, with Murata Manufacturing ( MRAAF ) jumping 14.6%, Advantest ( ADTTF ) rising 13.2% and Tokyo Electron ( TOELF ) surging 11.4%. Data-centre suppliers such as Furukawa Electric ( FUWAF ) advanced 13.15% and Mitsui Kinzoku ( XZJCF ) gained 9.33%.

The market breadth was positive, with 158 advancers on the Nikkei index against 64 decliners, while 3 stocks were flat.

Shares of Nvidia ( NVDA ), a bellwether for the AI sector, surged 31.5% overnight in their biggest one-day percentage gain since May 9, 2003.

The chipmaker had announced Huang's resignation on November 12 following revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving an alleged Chinese spy, a development that helped trigger last week's global equity selloff.

At the same time, analysts say Huang's return does not mean uncertainties surrounding restrictions on data-centre construction will be eased, nor does it improve the profitability of AI investment.

"Uncertainty has actually increased over how much tighter restrictions on China could become going forward," said Shingo Ide, chief equity strategist at NLI Research Institute.

"Whether it's restrictions on data-centre construction or export controls on China, these issues could drag on for six months to a year. During that time, the market will likely swing back and forth on comments from key officials and various headlines."

(Reporting by Satoshi Sugiyama; Editing by Subhranshu Sahu and Sherry Jacob-Phillips)

data.title: Meta Platforms Pauses Class C Share Issuance During Recapitalization Lawsuit
data.description:
07:59 PM EST, 11/23/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Meta Platforms Inc ( META ) said Monday it will not issue Class C shares while pretrial and trial proceedings continue in a shareholder lawsuit challenging its recapitalization, according to a filing.

The trial is scheduled to begin April 19, 2027. CEO Mark Zuckerberg waived a deadline requiring the company to pay a previously declared Class C stock dividend within five business days after its amended certificate of incorporation takes effect, the filing said.

Meta said it does not expect to launch its previously announced at-the-market stock program until after the dividend is paid.

The waiver expires under specified conditions, including June 30, 2027, if the dividend has not been paid by then.

data.description:
BOGOTA, Nov 23 (Reuters) - Colombia's National Environmental Licensing Authority (ANLA) on Monday granted licenses to two hydrocarbon projects in the eastern part of the country, allowing them to move forward to the exploration, production and exploitation phases.

The Petroleos Colombianos' Campo Tapir Sureste project in the eastern department of Casanare received an environmental license to proceed with exploration and production involving drilling up to 35 conventional wells across five locations.

ANLA also approved the modification of a license for the CPO-5 exploratory drilling area in the department of Meta to a production license for the project, to be led by ONGC Videsh's Colombia arm and GeoPark ( GPRK ).

data.title: Fed's Williams says inflation still too high, signals more rate hikes possible
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov 23 (Reuters) - New York Federal Reserve President John Williams said on Monday that persistently high inflation continues to point the US central bank toward tighter monetary policy, while stressing that the pace of future interest-rate increases will depend on incoming economic data.

"We must take actions over time that will ensure that we get inflation back to our 2% goal in a timely manner and on a sustained basis," Williams said in remarks at an event held by the University of Mount Saint Vincent in New York. "There is still work to do to get that done." 

Williams said inflation is "too high." He noted that he will continue to assess incoming data to decide what action the central bank should take at its December 8-9 policy meeting.

Williams' comments suggested he favors a rate hike at the upcoming meeting. Beyond that, Williams said the path of policy will depend on the economy's performance. "I don't have in my mind a particular timing," Williams told reporters. 

"We're going to have to learn along the way as we get more data," Williams said, while noting, "I'm not excluding options" when it comes to the cadence of future actions. "I would not exclude, you know, moving at consecutive meetings at all if that was what was needed." 

If the economy showed considerable strength and inflation pressures were not moderating, "you wouldn't just want to wait around" and would instead act by adjusting monetary policy, the official said.

DECEMBER HIKE AHOY

Financial markets broadly expect the Fed to raise its policy rate by a quarter of a percentage point next month from the current 3.75%-4.00% range, with more increases to come next year.

The Fed last raised rates in September as part of an effort to curb inflation, which has been above the 2% target for more than five years. Central bank officials worry that, if this situation persists, the public could lose confidence that inflation will return to that level.

Over recent weeks a wide range of Fed officials have pointed to the need for more rate hikes. Some policymakers have said they'd like to see increases come gradually to allow the economy to adjust, while Fed Governor Christopher Waller has signaled he could support a more aggressive half-percentage-point increase given hot price pressure data. 

Williams was speaking the same day as a sharp stock market rally, triggered by chipmaker Nvidia's ( NVDA ) announcement that it was reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO, after President Donald Trump urged it to do so. Investors' reaction highlighted the importance of AI companies in driving the markets. Some observers had wondered in recent days whether sharp stock losses might deter the Fed from raising rates.

Williams told reporters he was not surprised by the market's volatility and he said that thus far what's happened had not dimmed his optimism about the future of the economy.

Williams also said in his formal remarks that he expects inflation to end the year at 3.5% and to moderate to just above 2% next year before easing to the target in 2028. He also noted that risks to inflation continue to be skewed to the upside and said among the key drivers of high price pressures, energy prices remain elevated and the outlook on that front is uncertain.

He added that "although the effects of tariffs, geopolitical conflicts, and the AI surge are showing up in prices of certain categories of goods, there is little evidence of these spilling over significantly into broader and more persistent inflation."

Williams also said the economy is showing strength and resilience and should grow by 2.75% in both 2026 and 2027. He added that the job market has been showing stability, and the current 4.1% unemployment rate should fall to around 4% next year.

(Reporting by Michael S. Derby; Editing by Paul Simao and Diane Craft)

data.title: Japan's factory activity expands in November, PMI shows
data.description:
TOKYO, Nov 24 (Reuters) - Japan's manufacturing activity grew at a slightly faster in November as output and export orders picked up on semiconductor and electronics demand, a preliminary business survey showed on Tuesday.

-- The S&P Global Flash Japan Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index rose to 53.7 in November from 53.3 in October, a preliminary survey by S&P Global showed. The 50-mark separates growth from contraction.

-- A key sub-index for factory output grew and new orders rose at a solid pace helped by a sharp rise in export orders.

-- New export orders accelerated from October thanks to robust demand, especially from other major Asian economies. This lifted new export business at the overall private sector at the fastest rate since January 2018.

data.title: Explainer-What are the various US federal and state probes faced by Nvidia and Jensen Huang?
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 23 (Reuters) - As President Donald Trump welcomed Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO and declared the tech billionaire's return posed no national security risk, the company and its boss faced a host of state and federal probes and reviews.

Here are details on some of those actions, with their status in certain cases remaining unclear:

FBI AND US INTELLIGENCE REVIEWS:

After reports that the Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO had an extramarital affair with unrelated Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, whom US intelligence agencies probed over whether she was a Chinese asset, Trump said on November 9 the FBI was "looking into" the issue.

Jensen Huang has acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife and apologized, but has not ​publicly addressed the situation further. China has denied the espionage allegations.

US intelligence agencies examined the extent of the Chinese businesswoman's ties to China's Ministry of State Security and what information she may have passed to Beijing, people familiar with the matter have told Reuters.

When asked after the Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO's reinstatement what the CIA had told Trump, the president told CNBC: "Let me just say, I have clearance. And if I didn't have clearance, I wouldn't have done ​the deal (with Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board for Jensen Huang's return)."

Trump said Attorney General Todd Blanche confirmed the federal government has no evidence that Huang engaged in unlawful conduct.

The New York Times reported that Alice Huang kept in contact with an official from China's top spy agency for more than a year during the affair. China's foreign ministry has previously said the spy accusations were "groundless," and Reuters has been unable to determine Alice Huang's whereabouts to seek comment.

Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board has formed a committee to investigate ​whether foreign intelligence efforts targeted Jensen Huang and is also starting a search to name a new chief compliance officer. 

ANTITRUST PROBE:

The Justice Department has also been reviewing Nvidia's ( NVDA ) $12.9 billion deal to buy open-source platform Hugging Face alongside a broader antitrust investigation into the company's acquisitions and practices, Reuters reported in October.

The ‌Justice Department's recent questioning covers Nvidia's ( NVDA ) acquisitions, investments, sales practices, and whether the chip designer has exerted pressure on its customers, people familiar with the matter said in October.

The Justice Department has also scrutinized Nvidia's ( NVDA ) ​conduct following other transactions, including ⁠its 2025 deal to license technology from chip startup Groq and hire its engineers, Reuters has reported. 

Officials have explored whether Nvidia ( NVDA ) unfairly offered larger allocations of AI chips if customers purchased its networking equipment and Groq processors, raising questions about whether Nvidia ( NVDA ) used its dominant product to push into a newer market.

Nvidia ( NVDA ), which is a cornerstone ​of the tech economy and AI boom, has declined to comment on the probes.

SEC PROBE:

The US Securities and Exchange Commission is probing Nvidia's ( NVDA ) accounting practices, Reuters reported on November 20, citing two people briefed on the matter.

Reuters could not immediately determine when the SEC opened its ​inquiry or exactly what potential accounting issues the watchdog examined. 

Analysts and investors have grown increasingly concerned about circular AI financing deals, in which chipmakers including Nvidia ( NVDA ) have pursued complex financial arrangements to help customers fund purchases of their chips and the construction of costly AI infrastructure, such as data centers. 

Nvidia ( NVDA ) has backed AI companies and cloud providers ​and provided guarantees connected to data-center projects that use its equipment. Critics say such arrangements can make it harder for investors to assess ​the quality of chipmakers' revenue ⁠and their true financial exposure. 

On its November 17 earnings call, Nvidia's ( NVDA ) then-interim CEO Colette Kress said the company was proud of its role in supporting the AI industry, but would be far more ⁠selective about future AI industry financing deals.

CALIFORNIA STATE PROBE:

California Attorney General Rob Bonta said on November 19 his office had served an investigative subpoena to Nvidia ( NVDA ) related to reports of Huang's affair with the Chinese businesswoman.

The probe will help determine whether Nvidia's ( NVDA ) actions violated California law, the attorney general's office said.

CONGRESSIONAL PROBES:

Democrats, who will hold a majority in the House of Representatives and the Senate from January following the November midterm elections, have been very critical of Huang and Nvidia ( NVDA ) and of Huang's ties to the Republican president. US ‌lawmakers from both parties sharply criticized Nvidia's ( NVDA ) decision to reinstate Huang as CEO.

"Democrats will wield their full power to investigate any wrongdoing by the Trump Administration, Jensen Huang, other Nvidia ( NVDA ) executives, and anyone selling out our national security for financial gain," top Senate Democrat Chuck Schumer said after Huang was reinstated.

Top House Democrat Hakeem Jeffries said Congress will "not be deterred from conducting a swift, thorough and wide-ranging investigation into business malfeasance by Nvidia ( NVDA )."

Huang has voiced support for Trump's AI agenda and met the Republican leader many times as Nvidia ( NVDA ) has sought to sell advanced chips to the ‌Chinese market and lobbied for looser restrictions on Chinese access to Nvidia's ( NVDA ) sophisticated AI chips.

Democratic and Republican lawmakers have called to halt exports of advanced AI chips to China. Huang and the White House have argued that continuing US sales to China would keep Chinese customers reliant on US technology.

Huang has agreed to testify before the US Senate in a public hearing on December 3, the Senate Banking Committee said.

The chairs of the House committees on China, intelligence and foreign affairs separately said Huang and Nvidia ( NVDA ) General Counsel Tim Teter have confirmed they will appear for transcribed interviews on December 1 and December 2 as previously planned.

MEGASPEED PROBES:

Democratic lawmakers have opened a probe into what influence Nvidia ( NVDA ) was able to wield over a US Commerce Department investigation of Singapore-based cloud-computing company Megaspeed for possible illegal diversion of chips to China, according ‌to a November 19 letter reviewed by Reuters. 

The Chinese businesswoman with whom the Nvidia ( NVDA ) boss had an affair is a former executive at Megaspeed, an Nvidia ( NVDA ) partner that operates data centers. Megaspeed said it complies with all applicable laws, including US ⁠export control ​requirements.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) said that as an American ​company it consults with department officials to answer questions, provide information and request guidance.

The Commerce and ​Justice departments released information on November 16 about Washington's investigation into Megaspeed, Nvidia's ( NVDA ) Asia-Pacific partner, which the departments said ‌began two years ago.

They said Commerce investigators requested records from Nvidia ( NVDA ) ​in May 2025 about sales to the company and, with Singaporean authorities, conducted an ​on-site inspection in June 2025 at Megaspeed and interviewed Alice Huang.

Washington added Megaspeed to its trade blacklist on November 23.

data.title: US blacklists Megaspeed cloud company linked to Nvidia scandal
data.description:
* Megaspeed now needs Commerce Department approval for US exports, likely to be denied

* Commerce adds six linked companies from Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand to Entity List

* Democratic lawmakers this week open probe into Nvidia's ( NVDA ) influence over Commerce investigation

* Megaspeed is under investigation for allegedly diverting chips to China

By Karen Freifeld

WASHINGTON, Nov 23 (Reuters) - The US Commerce Department on Monday added Singapore-based Megaspeed, the cloud company at the center of the Nvidia ( NVDA ) scandal, to its trade blacklist, following criticism from lawmakers and administration officials.

Megaspeed, an Nvidia ( NVDA ) partner which has been under investigation by US authorities since 2024 over whether it diverted AI chips to China, will now need approval from the US Commerce Department to obtain US exports, which is likely to be denied.

"The Department of Commerce still needs to explain to Commerce why this took so long," Senator Pete Ricketts, a Nebraska Republican, said in a posting on X.

Megaspeed gained the spotlight about two weeks ago after news broke that Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, whom US authorities suspect of being a Chinese spy. China has said the spy accusations are "groundless."

After the news broke, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent publicly complained that the Commerce Department had not yet placed the company on its Entity List.

He also called out Nvidia ( NVDA ). "The real story here should be: Did Nvidia know their client and was there a robust effort at Nvidia ( NVDA ) to make sure that there was no leakage and that they were selling to what were obviously pass-through shell companies?" Bessent told CNBC's "Squawk Box" program.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) has said it recently formed an export control committee to oversee trade compliance and national security risks.

Megaspeed did not immediately return a request for comment. A week ago, the company issued a statement saying it conducts legitimate and lawful business, including complying with US export controls.

It also said Alice Huang officially left Megaspeed in August 2025.

The US Justice Department and Commerce Department issued a joint statement last week saying they would "bring the full extent of the law against Megaspeed for any criminal conduct that may have occurred."

Democratic lawmakers this week opened a probe into what influence Nvidia ( NVDA ) was able to wield over the Commerce Department's investigation.

Besides Megaspeed International Pte in Singapore, the Commerce Department on Monday added six other companies from Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand to the Entity List. All had some link to Megaspeed, a Commerce official said.

The blacklisting coincided with Jensen Huang's reinstatement as CEO of Nvidia ( NVDA ) after his resignation two weeks ago.

The last time the Commerce Department placed any new entities on the list was October 2025.

As Reuters exclusively reported in June, the US has held off adding China's AI startup DeepSeek, memory chipmaker CXMT and more than 100 other companies flagged as national security risks to the trade blacklist, as the Trump administration tried to avoid escalating tensions with Beijing.

(Reporting by Chris Sanders and Karen Freifeld; Editing by Tom Hogue, Alistair Bell and Stephen Coates)

data.title: Trump flexes influence after midterm losses with intervention at Nvidia
data.description:
* Trump says administration found no national security problem with Huang's return

* Democrats vow investigations after taking control of Congress in January

* Move extends Trump's history of intervening in strategic corporate boardroom and deal decisions

(Updates throughout with context, analysis)

By Doina Chiacu and Steve Holland

WASHINGTON, Nov 23 (Reuters) - President Donald Trump's intervention to restore Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia ( NVDA ) offered an early indication of how Trump, despite losing control of Congress to Democrats, can continue to wield power in Washington and beyond during what is traditionally considered the lame-duck phase of any presidency.

Days after the Nvidia ( NVDA ) board had ruled out restoring Huang following a series of damaging revelations about his relations with an alleged Chinese spy and other women, Trump seized control of the narrative.

He forcefully made the case for Huang's return in a press conference on Friday, then dispatched key members of his administration throughout the weekend to convince the board to reverse its position in an announcement shortly before the stock market opened on Monday.

Trump celebrated his victory with nearly an hour-long interview on CNBC in which he took credit for the turnabout and called Huang a "national treasure."

"The board decided to do what we wanted to do. And one of the things the board wanted to know: Is there a national security problem?" Trump told CNBC.

"And after a lot of research... we said, 'No, it's not a problem,'" Trump said. "We feel very strongly that he's in good shape, very good shape."

The stock market soared. Members of Congress complained. Meanwhile, Trump - just weeks from his party's historic midterm election blowout that many Republicans blamed on his falling popularity - was back at the center of the world's gaze.

He soon made a social media post, based on a photo of his own triumphant fist pump following his near-assassination at a Pennsylvania political rally in 2024, but with Huang superimposed where Trump stood in the original. In Huang's hand dangled a red bra, an apparent reference to the sex scandal he had just escaped, aided by Trump's unusual knack for bending storylines to his desires.

"He's willing to do things in a very unorthodox manner," said presidential historian Thomas Alan Schwartz of Vanderbilt University. "Getting Huang back as CEO is clearly in the category of unorthodox."

NATIONAL SECURITY CONCERNS REMAIN

It was not the first time Trump has inserted himself into major corporate decisions, having pushed deals involving Intel ( INTC ) and U.S. Steel. But his intervention with Nvidia ( NVDA ) went further by putting him directly into a boardroom decision over who should lead a trillion-dollar American corporation at the center of the global artificial intelligence race.

Trump's actions may yet boomerang. Democrats, who will have the widest majorities in decades to work with, vowed to investigate once they take control of Congress in January. Huang is scheduled to make a first round of testimony at a hearing next week.

Some of Trump's fellow Republicans joined Democrats on Monday in expressing fears that Huang's return posed a national security risk because of his relationship with the woman suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence.

"No national security risk? Based on what?" Republican Senator John Cornyn of Texas wrote on X. Cornyn was one of several Republicans who lost their seats after Trump backed rivals in primary elections.

Newt Gingrich, a former speaker of the US House of Representatives who is a close Trump ally, said on X, "There is something profoundly wrong" about Huang being reinstated.

"Congress should really dig into this as a national security issue of enormous proportions and also a significant failure in the federal bureaucracy," he said.

A BROADER PATTERN

Trump's intervention in corporate America has become a hallmark of his administration, particularly with companies considered important to US economic and national security.

After a public campaign from Trump and other members of his administration to block Nippon Steel's ( NISTF ) bid to buy U.S. Steel in a $14.9-billion acquisition, the Japanese company agreed to give an unusual degree of power to Trump over the company's future. The administration gained the authority to name a board member, as well as the last word on idling plants, production cuts and moving jobs overseas.

Trump's team also negotiated a 10% stake in Intel ( INTC ) last year under a deal with the struggling chipmaker that converted government grants into an equity share. Trump had called for the resignation of Intel ( INTC ) CEO Lip-Bu Tan over his ties to China before announcing a deal that made the US government the biggest shareholder in the chipmaker.

The administration also struck an agreement allowing Nvidia ( NVDA ) to sell its H20 chips to China in exchange for receiving 15% of those sales and an agreement for the Pentagon to become the largest shareholder in a small mining company, MP Materials ( MP ) , to boost output of rare earth magnets.

(Reporting by Doina Chiacu, Steve Holland, Susan Heavey, Katharine Jackson, Patricia Zengerle in Washington; Ananya Palyekar, Hyunsu Yim and Harishankar Manoj in Bangalore; Editing by Craig Timberg and Cynthia Osterman)

data.title: Analysis-Huang's stunning Nvidia return sparks relief for battered AI trade
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov 23 (Reuters) - For US stock investors, Monday's stunning return of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang brought a sigh of relief for the battered AI trade, one worth trillions of dollars in market value.

Huang's reinstatement atop the semiconductor giant halted a severe slide in technology shares that had sent the benchmark S&P 500 into a correction amid growing doubts about the AI trade that had been the primary engine for the four-year-old bull stock market.

The reversal by Nvidia's board in bringing back Huang came after his abrupt departure earlier this month rattled an already anxious market. Concerns flared not only about Nvidia but also about the health of the AI ecosystem which the chip company has been at the center of. 

"You've basically had this perfect storm of uncertainty that has created a crisis of confidence," said King Lip, chief strategist at BakerAvenue Wealth Management in San Francisco. "This Nvidia fallout was one of those pieces of ...uncertainty. So this removes a pretty significant one with Jensen coming back."

Shares of Nvidia soared on news of Huang's return to the company he co-founded, rising 32% in early afternoon trading, equivalent to more than $900 billion in market capitalization added back to the value of the semiconductor company, whose stock price has been hammered in recent weeks.

Shares of companies across the AI industry rallied sharply, with the Nasdaq 100 that is concentrated in megacap tech companies jumping more than 6%.

"The initial reaction here is a big collective sigh of relief," said Thomas Urano, co-chief investment officer at Sage Advisory in Austin, Texas. "Maybe Jensen...puts confidence back in the AI trade."

Many investors had worried about the extent to which Nvidia's massive value was tied up in Huang, who was credited for foreseeing the technology shift that led to Nvidia's advanced chips that are central to the AI boom and to Nvidia's soaring profits.

Nvidia's chief financial officer Colette Kress had been running the company on an interim basis while the company searched for a permanent replacement. 

"To try to replace Jensen was something that nobody could feel comfortable that they are going to find somebody to automatically fill his shoes," said Tom Plumb, portfolio manager of the Plumb Balanced Fund in Madison, Wisconsin. "But to have the visionary who was able to attract some of the most talented people in the industry ... it's certainly very, very positive for the company."

Huang has been "essentially the product manager of his company," said Kim Forrest, chief investment officer at Bokeh Capital Partners. "And that's really important, which is why a lot of investors are happy to see him back."

More broadly, Nvidia has been tied to an array of companies involved in the sprawling AI buildout. Many investors had voiced concerns about the future of that ecosystem without Huang himself, who is seen as one of the most pivotal AI figures.

Some investors also said Huang's return could clear some regulatory clouds over the stock. Huang's resignation followed revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged spy for China. 

President Donald Trump, who said he secured the deal to bring back Huang, said in a post on Truth Social the US government had no reason to believe Huang's return posed a national security risk and had no evidence he had engaged in unlawful conduct.

Trump told CNBC that the stock market reaction to Huang's resignation from Nvidia "probably" factored into his decision to push for the CEO's reinstatement although his view of the long-term benefit of having Huang at the helm of the company was the bigger weight. 

Some regulatory clouds could remain. California's attorney general's office said on Monday that Huang's reinstatement does not diminish the need for a probe into what Nvidia told investors about its China ties.

And questions about the AI trade that had dogged the market before the Nvidia crisis erupted were likely to persist.

Those questions center around the sustainability of massive AI spending on data centers and other infrastructure, which has driven up profits for a broad swath of companies.

Concerns have grown about financing of those investments and whether they will generate sufficient returns. Meanwhile, a sweeping Democratic victory in the midterm elections earlier this month is driving expectations of stronger political pushback against the development of data centers in the US.

"We very well may see more selling pressure after this relief rally runs its course," said James St. Aubin, chief investment officer at Ocean Park Asset Management in Santa Monica, California. "Jensen's return doesn't answer the big questions investors were grappling with."

(Reporting by Lewis Krauskopf, Chibuike Oguh and Chuck Mikolajczak, additional reporting by Anand Gopal; Editing by Megan Davies and Alistair Bell)

data.title: NEWSMAKER-Jensen Huang's comeback to Nvidia underscores his outsized grip on AI
data.description:
* Board reinstates Huang in sharp reversal amid mounting pressure from Trump, shareholders

* Markets, top AI CEOs cheer return of Huang, central to AI trade

* Trump says his 'intervention' was key to bringing Huang back

(Rewrites with Huang reinstatement and quotes from Trump, analysts; adds fresh background)

By Deborah Mary Sophia, Anhata Rooprai and Aditya Soni

Nov 23 (Reuters) - Jensen Huang made a triumphant return to Nvidia's ( NVDA ) Santa Clara, California, headquarters on Monday, less than two weeks after he resigned as CEO following revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged spy for China.

Clad in his trademark black leather jacket, hand on heart, the 63-year-old CEO smiled at cheering employees who packed an atrium and crowded the balconies above.

US President Donald Trump - instrumental in Huang's comeback - heaped praise and fellow tech icon Elon Musk hailed his return. Nvidia shares surged 31.5%, propelling a broader Wall Street rally.

Huang's swift reinstatement at the helm of the chipmaker he co-founded more than three decades ago is the story of a stunning comeback, one that underscores his sway over Washington, markets, the AI industry and geopolitics.

"Jensen is bigger than Elvis for tech investors," said Eric Schiffer, chairman of Los Angeles-based private equity firm Patriarch Organization.

A linchpin of the AI boom, Huang's role extends beyond that of Nvidia's ( NVDA ) CEO. Cultivating relationships with lawmakers, partners, customers and suppliers across the globe, Huang has bankrolled the industry's massive buildout. Billionaires like Oracle Chairman Larry Ellison and Musk have resorted to "begging Jensen for GPUs," Ellison said in 2024.

Treated like a rock star in Asia, Huang has been mobbed by fans on the streets of Taipei and Seoul, asking for his autograph on books, posters and even on their bodies.

But even with his dramatic comeback, questions remain about the big checks Huang wrote for AI startups, which in turn bought Nvidia chips.

Before he resigned, Huang was already facing calls to dial down the practice of supporting Nvidia's ( NVDA ) growth with the company's own cash flow, which many on Wall Street warned created a risky web of circular financing. Huang had pushed back on that critique, saying Nvidia was financing genuine demand.

His exit had called into question whether the AI ecosystem and companies like CoreWeave ( CRWV ) and Nebius would continue to thrive without Huang. Their stocks surged on Monday.

"You can see how one man was so much the face of this industry. He leaves and the whole place goes to heck in a handbag. And all of a sudden, he's back and everything is rebounding," said Bill Gunderson, partner at GCG Advisory Partners.

'TOO BIG TO FIRE'

Huang is Nvidia's ( NVDA ) fifth-largest shareholder with a roughly 3.6% stake, but does not have special voting shares that give founders such as Meta Platforms' ( META ) Mark Zuckerberg and SpaceX's Musk effective control of their companies.

Huang is known for his hands-on management style, personally delving into problems at Nvidia and overseeing some 60 direct reports, nearly all in engineering roles, including experts in memory chips, networking and graphics and central processors.

"A lot of companies' organization charts, they all look the same. And it doesn't ​make any sense to me. The architecture ​of the company should reflect the environment ⁠in which it exists," Huang said on a podcast in March.

He has dug deep into the startups Nvidia has invested in, helping them secure customers and has even joined fundraising calls to attract investors, according to startup founders, venture capitalists and a former Nvidia employee.

Huang's influence was on display on Monday after Trump said he played a key role in bringing back Huang, throwing his weight behind the scandal-hit CEO. "He did nothing wrong," Trump said on Monday, calling Huang "a genius."

Huang's return stumped many and US lawmakers from both parties strongly objected to his reinstatement. But it also reinforced the idea that some tech CEOs were considered irreplaceable, a big risk for a company critical to the AI industry.

"When the CEO is too big to fire, the board's job isn't to fire him. It's to fence him in," said corporate governance and ethics professor Nada Kakabadse of Henley Business School in Britain.

(Reporting by Aditya Soni, Deborah Sophia and Anhata Rooprai in Bengaluru, Krystal Hu in San Francisco and Toby Sterling in Amsterdam; Writing by Sayantani Ghosh; Editing by Nick Zieminski and Jamie Freed)

data.title: CFTC finalises permanent data-reporting rules for event contracts
data.description:
Nov 23 (Reuters) - The US Commodity Futures Trading Commission finalized permanent data-reporting rules for certain event contracts on Monday, aiming to strengthen oversight of prediction markets.

-- The rule comes as prediction markets face growing regulatory scrutiny in the US, with questions over federal oversight and market integrity

-- The final rule creates an alternative reporting framework for certain fully collateralised event contracts that have operated under CFTC staff no-action relief since 2017

-- "The CFTC will no longer regulate market participants through a patchwork of no-action letters, which serve as band-aids for unworkable regulations. This final rule is an important step in future-proofing the regulatory framework for event contracts," Chairman Michael Selig said

-- Under the new framework, reporting markets, futures commission merchants, clearing members and foreign brokers will report data under Parts 15-18 of CFTC regulations, instead of relying on reporting provisions spread across Parts 38, 39, 43 and 45

-- The move follows other efforts by the regulator to strengthen federal oversight of prediction markets, including an earlier proposal to classify certain event contracts as swaps

(Reporting by Pritam Biswas in Bengaluru; Editing by Sherry Jacob-Phillips)

HOUSTON, TX / ACCESS Newswire / November 23, 2026 / XCF Global, Inc. ( SAFX ) ("XCF" or the "Company"), a U.S.-based producer of renewable diesel and sustainable aviation fuel, today outlined its continued focus on growing renewable fuel production, strengthening commercial performance and advancing its expansion strategy as it prepares for a planned transition to over-the-counter trading. On November 18, 2026, the Company received a notice from the Listing Qualifications Department of The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC ("Nasdaq") determining to delist XCF's Class A common stock from The Nasdaq Capital Market.

"We are building on tangible progress at Reno, where production increased each month during the third quarter and revenue grew 127% year over year," said Chris Cooper, XCF Global ( SAFX ) Chief Executive Officer. "With Southern Energy and DevvStream Corp. now part of XCF and a definitive agreement signed for the proposed Paramount acquisition, we have expanded our capabilities and established opportunities for future growth. Our priority is to convert that progress into consistent production, stronger customer relationships and improved cash generation. We remain confident in the opportunity to build a significant domestic renewable fuels business that supports American agriculture and energy security, and we are committed to earning shareholder confidence through execution and results."

XCF's operating progress provides a foundation for its next phase of development. Following the July restart at New Rise Renewables Reno, monthly renewable diesel production increased from approximately 0.55 million gallons in July to 1.01 million gallons in August and 1.35 million gallons in September. Commercial shipments increased 15.5% from August to September to 1.46 million gallons, and third-quarter 2026 revenue increased 127% year over year to $21.7 million.

In October, XCF completed its business combination with Southern Energy Renewables Inc. and DevvStream Corp., broadening its renewable fuel technology capabilities and adding expertise in environmental asset management and monetization. The Company also signed a definitive agreement to acquire the Paramount, California renewable fuel refinery. The proposed acquisition remains subject to closing conditions, financing and other requirements.

Building on these developments, XCF is focused on improving production consistency and commercial performance at Reno, advancing planning for Paramount and evaluating additional renewable fuel development opportunities. A timely hearing request would not stay the suspension of trading in the Company's Class A common stock. The Company does not intend to request a hearing.

However, the Company is working to facilitate quotation of its common stock on the over-the-counter market following the Nasdaq suspension and intends to pursue the highest OTC market tier for which it qualifies, which we expect will be OTCID. The timing of OTC quotation, applicable market tier and trading symbol will be announced when confirmed. There can be no assurance regarding the timing or availability of OTC quotation or qualification for any particular market tier.

data.title: US Medicare says price cuts on 13 more drugs will reduce spending by 45%
data.description:
Nov 23 (Reuters) - The US Medicare health plan on Monday said new, lower prices for 13 of its costliest drugs, including Gilead's HIV treatment Biktarvy and Eli Lilly's ( LLY ) diabetes drug Trulicity, will cut costs by 45% compared with recent annual spending on those medicines, or about $9.2 billion.

The price reductions, which take effect in 2028, are the third annual round of negotiated cuts under the former Biden administration's Inflation Reduction Act of 2022. Medicare, the federal health plan covering over 67 million people aged 65 and over, was previously barred by law from negotiating prices with drugmakers.

"The Trump administration is committed to use every tool at our disposal to negotiate fairer, more affordable prices to ease the burden on Medicare beneficiaries," Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services Administrator Mehmet Oz said in a statement.

The agency said its monthly price for Biktarvy will be cut by 37%, while Trulicity will be 84% lower. Overall, the price reductions range from 34% to 84%.

Gilead warned last month that Medicare's new "maximum fair price" of $2,600 for a month's supply of Biktarvy would reduce sales of the drug by about $1.5 billion, although the drugmaker still expects overall HIV revenue to increase compared to 2027.

Medicare said two drugs previously selected for negotiation, Pfizer's ( PFE ) arthritis treatment Xeljanz and Roche's asthma drug Xolair, were exempted from the program because they already have generic competition.

The agency also said AbbVie's ( ABBV ) Botox will not be subject to a maximum fair price due to a court order.

Despite the pharmaceutical industry's longstanding opposition to the law and multiple failed lawsuits, the first negotiated prices on 10 drugs sold in pharmacies went into effect this year.

The 2028 list also includes products that are administered in doctors' offices or hospitals, such as Novartis' psoriasis drug Cosentyx and Takeda's Entyvio for Crohn's disease. Novartis' breast cancer drug Kisqali and antidepressant Rexulti, sold by Otsuka Pharmaceutical and Lundbeck, are also among the 13 medicines with lower Medicare prices.

Medicare said the selected drugs accounted for $22.3 billion in spending in 2025. The drugs are also selected based on being either 7 or 11 years out from being approved by the US Food and Drug Administration and for which there is no generic or biosimilar alternative.

Medicare said last year that the prices it had negotiated for 15 drugs starting in 2027, including Novo Nordisk's GLP-1 drug Ozempic, would save the program 36% on those medications compared with recent annual spending, or about $8.5 billion.

(Reporting By Deena Beasley in Los Angeles; Editing by Bill Berkrot)

New locations across 11 states will provide healthcare professionals with continued access to scrubs, uniforms, and in-store shopping. 

FORT LAUDERDALE, Fla., Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Uniform Advantage has finalized the acquisition of 16 former Scrubs and Beyond retail locations, marking a significant expansion of its brick-and-mortar presence acr Uniform Advantage, a leading retailer of medical uniforms and accessories, has acquired 16 former Scrubs & Beyond retail locations, expanding its presence across the country and bringing the brand to eight new states.

The acquisition follows the closure of more than 115 Scrubs & Beyond stores by former parent company Kindthread. With many healthcare professionals losing access to their neighborhood uniform stores, Uniform Advantage saw an opportunity to keep these locations open and continue serving the communities that depend on them.

"For years, healthcare professionals have been asking us to open stores in their area, so when we learned that former Scrubs and Beyond locations were available, we saw a wonderful opportunity to make that happen in select markets. These stores let us bring our exclusive brands and other brands directly to local communities, where people can touch, feel, try on and see our garments in person and find the fit that works for them. We're thrilled to welcome these communities to Uniform Advantage," said Susan Masimore, CEO of Uniform Advantage.

The 16 locations bring Uniform Advantage into eight new states: Texas, Kansas, Washington, Arizona, Michigan, Missouri, Nebraska, and New Mexico, while expanding its existing presence in California, Florida, and Georgia.

As part of the transition, Uniform Advantage made every effort to retain existing store employees, recognizing the relationships they have built with local healthcare professionals over the years. While not every team member will remain, the company has worked to preserve as much of that experience and local knowledge as possible.

More Brands, More Styles, More Choices 
The stores are now transitioning to the Uniform Advantage brand, with new merchandise arriving regularly. Customers will begin seeing a broader selection of scrubs, styles, colors, and sizes as the company builds out each location's assortment through March 2027. During the transition, product selection may vary by location.

Shoppers can look forward to Uniform Advantage's exclusive brands, including Butter-Soft, Easy STRETCH, and Hypothesis, alongside popular national brands such as Cherokee, Healing Hands, Med Couture, Grey's Anatomy, and Skechers.

For Uniform Advantage, the expansion builds on more than 40 years of serving healthcare professionals. What began as a single Florida store in 1985 has grown into a national retail and e-commerce business, with a continued focus on helping healthcare workers find uniforms that fit their needs, their style, and their demanding workdays.

To find a store near you, including addresses and hours, visit uniformadvantage.com/stores.

Founded in 1985, Uniform Advantage is a leading retailer of medical uniforms, scrubs, footwear, and accessories. Through its retail stores and online shopping experience, the company offers healthcare professionals a wide selection of exclusive and national brands designed for comfort, performance, and personal style.

data.title: Taiwan's Stock Pickers Are Walking Out to Bet Their Own Money
data.description:
NEW YORK, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fly On Wall Street News Commentary - Taiwan's benchmark stock index was up 62% this year, the best showing of any major equity gauge in the world, when Bloomberg reported on Oct. 16 that some of the island's professional fund managers and analysts are quitting their jobs to invest their own money. Strict rules keep them from trading the very stocks they pick for clients, and in a year when about one in ten stocks in the index has more than doubled, some have decided the trade-off is no longer worth it. Companies and funds mentioned in this article include: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited ( TSM ) [TSMC] , ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. ( ASX ) [ASE] , United Microelectronics Corporation ( UMC ) [UMC] , iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF , The Taiwan Fund, Inc. ( TWN ) .

Watching From Behind the Locker

Taiwan does not ban personal investing outright, but its asset-management code of conduct bars staff from trading a locally listed stock or a linked derivative within seven business days before or after their firm's funds trade it, which in practice rules out personal stock-picking. Fund managers must also lock away their phones, laptops and smartwatches each morning until the market closes at 1:30 p.m. The phone rule was formalized in 2024 to deter insider trading, the Taipei Times reported in July, after six former fund managers from four firms were indicted for front-running trades through the accounts of relatives and friends.

Ken Tsai, 40, a fund manager who until July worked at a large Taiwanese asset manager that Bloomberg did not name, told Bloomberg he made a Taiwanese maker of AI-server data-transfer components his fund's largest holding in 2024. The stock rose more than fivefold in 2025 and about sixfold again this year, but he owned none of it personally. "It left me with a strong sense of relative deprivation," he said. He now works at a private investment firm in Taipei, which was also not named. Pay adds to the pull: Taiwan portfolio managers earn roughly US$124,000 to US$311,000 a year, well below Hong Kong base salaries, according to Bloomberg, citing headhunters and recruitment-firm data.

The private shops they are joining sit outside those rules. They register as private companies with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and do not need asset-management licenses from the Financial Supervisory Commission because they do not raise public money. Brokers told Bloomberg some of them now generate more than NT$10 billion in monthly trading volume, rivaling mid-sized asset managers.

The Rally Behind the Exits

Much of the rally traces back to the AI hardware supply chain. TSMC reported third-quarter revenue of NT$1.49 trillion (US$46.7 billion) on Oct. 15, up 50.9% from a year earlier, while net income jumped 68.7% and gross margin reached 66.4%. It guided fourth-quarter revenue from US$52.3 billion to US$54.3 billion.

Chip packaging and testing has ridden the same wave. ASE Technology ( ASX ) reported September net revenue of NT$88.1 billion, up 45.5% from a year earlier, and third-quarter revenue of NT$244.2 billion, up 44.8%.

Mature-node foundry UMC reported August sales up 30.71% from a year earlier, lifting year-to-date sales 14.66%. In its second-quarter report, the company guided for capacity utilization above 90% in the third quarter and said revenue from its 22/28nm business continues to set record highs.

CONTINUED... Read more market coverage at: flyonwallstreet.com

A Talent Squeeze, Not a Stampede

The numbers point to churn more than an exodus. Fewer than half of Taiwan's 20 largest local equity mutual funds have kept the same portfolio manager for more than three years, according to fund-data site MoneyDJ, and Bloomberg reported that applications for junior roles at some international firms have roughly halved this year. Yet the FSC said the industry's registered headcount actually rose to 4,729 in September from 4,581 at the end of 2025. Firms are responding: the largest foreign asset manager in Taiwan is offering cross-market analyst roles and office rotations to keep staff.

Regulators are paying attention. The FSC said on Oct. 15 it is gathering information and plans to review the rules, balancing market development against conflicts of interest and investor protection. One asset-management executive told Bloomberg there is no easy solution for now.

The Case for the Pros

At least one professionally managed fund has kept pace. The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ), a closed-end fund listed in New York, reported a 47.36% total return for its fiscal quarter ended May 31, against 26.12% for the TAIEX Total Return Index over the same period, with net asset value of US$116.90 a share at the end of that quarter.

Investors who prefer to own the whole market can use the iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF, which holds about US$11.9 billion in assets.

Last week was a reminder of how quickly the math can change. The TAIEX fell 4.6%, its first weekly decline in five weeks, as a technology selloff spread and TSMC CEO C.C. Wei warned of macroeconomic uncertainty and weak consumer demand, according to Trading Economics. In New York, TSMC's shares fell 8.98% from the Oct. 9 close to $412.61 on Oct. 16, ASE dropped 14.86% to $39.53, UMC slid 13.68% to $19.82, the iShares fund lost 7.04% to $106.26 and The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ) declined 8.78% to $94.18, according to Stock Analysis data. For the managers who just traded a salary for their own account, those swings now land on them.

05:28 PM EST, 11/23/2026 (MT Newswires) -- (Updates with index/price moves, macroeconomic data, and company news from the first paragraph.)

US equity indexes jumped after Nvidia's ( NVDA ) decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive officer injected life into the so-called AI trade, whistling past outrage from Democrats.

The Nasdaq Composite soared 5.6% to 24,089.56 on Monday's close, after trading close to bear-market territory at the end of last week. The S&P 500 catapulted 4.7% to 7,237.17, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 3% to 49,595.31. Both the S&P 500 and the Dow had fallen into correction territory on Friday.

All sectors except energy and consumer staples rose. Technology was up 9%, followed by communication services and consumer discretionary.

"The [US] government has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to Nvidia ( NVDA ) poses any risk to national security," US President Donald Trump said in a social media post. "The Attorney General of the [US] has confirmed that the US government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct."

Nvidia's ( NVDA ) shares shot up over 31%, the top performer on the S&P 500, the Nasdaq, and the Dow.

Nvidia's ( NVDA ) success is driven less by its chips' performance and more by its "culture of innovation, ecosystem of incumbency, and massive investment in software, models, and services," according to a Truist Securities note. The culture of innovation was driven by Huang's "technical brilliance and magnetic personality," but the "downside/risks that remain are legal/regulatory," the note said.

Shares of CoreWeave ( CRWV ) and Nebius ( NBIS ) soared more than 22% and 20%, respectively, among the biggest Nasdaq gainers, as Huang's return eases the circular-financing risk surrounding neocloud companies with relatively high levels of debt.

The VanEck Semiconductor Exchange Traded Fund, with about $66.44 billion in assets under management, blew past 15%, reflecting strength in the AI trade.

At its quarterly earnings call in November, Nvidia ( NVDA ) told analysts it does not plan to bring Huang back as CEO. That course of action, however, changed on Monday.

"The board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia ( NVDA ), and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Chair Harvey Jones said in a statement on Monday. "The board received input from senior levels of the [US] government, and based on that input, the board is confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk."

"The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Huang, NVIDIA ( NVDA ) executives, and the company's board still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with US export controls," Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Ranking Member of the Senate Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee, said in a statement.

"The Trump Administration also needs to explain to Congress what 'input' was given and by which senior officials in the United States government to support his reinstatement," Warren said. "Huang's return only increases the urgency of passing bipartisan export control bills into law and making sure NVIDIA ( NVDA ) does not lobby to kill that legislation and put our national security at risk."

In economic news, S&P Global's November flash reading of manufacturing conditions fell to a three-month low of 54.5 from 54.9 in October, as expected in a Bloomberg-compiled survey.

In energy markets, the front-month West Texas Intermediate crude oil contract slumped 3.6% to $80.38 per barrel, while global benchmark Brent declined 3.4% to $89.46 per barrel.

In precious metals, gold futures jumped 3.3% to $3,631.4, and silver futures soared 4.5% to $42.90.

CrowdStrike ( CRWD ) shares slumped 8.9%, the worst performer on the SP 500 and the Nasdaq, after the company said Monday it has agreed to acquire Zscaler (ZS) in an all-stock deal valued at about $43.9 billion.

Arm (ARM) shares rose 16% after the company said CEO Rene Haas has agreed to remain in the role through 2033 under a new agreement.
